ADDENDUM 2026-08-06 (second thread, browser session). The `legislation.govt.nz` blocker described above is RESOLVED and the slice's load-bearing statutory chain has been re-read first-hand from the current consolidation, replacing the Wayback and FAOLEX proxy reads. The site renders normally in a browser; note for successors that its article-text extractor returns nothing, so the working route is DOM extraction against `div.prov`, and a session that only tries a text extractor will wrongly conclude the domain is dead. The chain, verified link by link and quoted verbatim: LGA 2002 s 111(1) "All information that is required by any provision of this Part or of Schedule 10 to be included in any plan, report, or other document must be prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting practice if that information is of a form or nature for which generally accepted accounting practice has developed standards." -> LGA 2002 s 5(1) "generally accepted accounting practice has the same meaning as in section 8 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013" -> FRA 2013 s 8 "In this Act, financial statements, group financial statements, a report, or other information complies with generally accepted accounting practice only if the report, statements, or information comply with— (a) applicable financial reporting standards; and (b) in relation to matters for which no provision is made in applicable financial reporting standards, an authoritative notice." -> FRA 2013 s 5(1) "financial reporting standard means a financial reporting standard issued by the Board under section 12" and "Board means the External Reporting Board continued under section 11". The chain therefore terminates in the XRB by statutory definition, as `G.1.md` claimed, and the claim no longer rests on a proxy read of any kind. IMPORTANT VERSION POINT: the earlier LGA 2002 read was of a reprint as at 26 March 2020; this read is of the current consolidation, and s 111(2) ("Subsection (1) does not apply to the preparation of a funding impact statement", added 27 November 2010) is present and unchanged. Cheap check 5 of `NZ/G.3.md` is closed. What remains unverified is the exhaustive Schedule 10 sweep, which is still a subagent's grep — see the `_dropped` entry for it.

reports.title: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand
reports.description: The audited annual financial statements of the whole New Zealand government reporting entity, presented to Parliament as paper B.11. New Zealand's analog of Canada's Public Accounts. Prepared under the Public Finance Act 1989 and NZ GAAP as defined in the Financial Reporting Act 2013, on Public Sector PBE Accounting Standards Tier 1. The Treasury also publishes interim (monthly, year-to-date) financial statements through the year; `releases_per_year` counts the audited year-end set only.
reports.cadence_note: One audited year-end set (B.11), plus roughly eleven interim monthly year-to-date sets on the same basis; `releases_per_year` counts the audited set only, since the interim statements are the same document unaudited rather than a separate release.

entries.covers: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand for the Year Ended 30 June 2026

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or statutory fixed date found on Treasury's site (legislation.govt.nz was inaccessible to confirm any Public Finance Act deadline). However, the audited year-end financial statements (B.11) have consistently been signed/issued in the first half of October each year: 5 Oct 2022 (FY2022), 5 Oct 2023 (FY2023), 10 Oct 2024 (FY2024), 9 Oct 2025 (FY2025). Next edition (FY ended 30 June 2026) is expected around early-to-mid October 2026 based on this pattern.

reports.title: Budget Economic and Fiscal Update
reports.description: The Treasury's Budget-day economic and fiscal forecasts, parliamentary paper B.3, required by the Public Finance Act 1989. Its forecasts become the 'Budget 20XX' comparatives in the following year's Financial Statements of the Government. A Half Year Economic and Fiscal Update (HYEFU) on the same statutory footing appears each December, and a Pre-election Update in election years; `releases_per_year` counts BEFU alone.
reports.cadence_note: BEFU annually in May; the companion HYEFU each December makes two statutory Updates a year, three in election years.

entries.covers: Budget 2027 BEFU (projected, exact Budget Day not yet announced)

release_schedule.note: BEFU is published annually alongside the government's Budget under the Public Finance Act 1989 (s26O), which requires a Budget Economic and Fiscal Update to accompany each year's Budget, but the Act does not fix a specific calendar date — Budget Day is set by the government each year. In practice Budget Day (and thus BEFU) has fallen in late May in every recent year observed (2024: 30 May; 2025: 22 May; 2026: 28 May, per Treasury's BEFU publication pages and Wikipedia's 2026 New Zealand budget article). No official date for Budget 2027 / BEFU 2027 had been announced as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Government finance statistics (general government)
reports.description: Stats NZ's annual consolidation of central and local government financial activity on the IMF's GFS framework — the direct counterpart of Australia's `au-abs-gfs`. Its own DataInfo+ metadata sets out a two-source split that is unusually explicit for this corpus: central government from the Treasury's CFISnet database, local government from the annual Local Authority Census supplemented by individual councils' annual reports.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ publishes this annual report each November covering the fiscal year ended the preceding June. The Year ended June 2025 edition was released 27 November 2025 and explicitly stated: "Government finance statistics (general government): Year ended June 2026 will be released in November 2026." No exact day was given, only the month.

reports.title: Local authority statistics (quarterly)
reports.description: Quarterly income and expenditure statistics for New Zealand's 11 regional councils and 68 territorial authorities, collected through the Quarterly Local Authority Survey (QLAS, questionnaire BS/QS/01). Provisional until benchmarked against the annual Local Authority Census, and fed forward into the national accounts and into Government finance statistics as the provisional local-government estimate.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ releases this report quarterly (March, June, September, December quarters). The March 2026 quarter release (published 10 June 2026, per its Mirage News mirror at https://www.miragenews.com/local-authority-statistics-march-2026-quarter-1689315/, which republishes the Stats NZ press release verbatim including the standard 'Next release' line) states: 'Local authority statistics: June 2026 quarter will be released on 7 September 2026.' The official stats.govt.nz page at the URL above corresponds to this same March 2026 quarter edition (confirmed reachable) but its full body text (including the next-release line) could not be extracted via the fetch tool, so the exact date is corroborated via the Mirage News mirror instead.

reports.title: Local Authority Census / Local Authority Financial Statistics
reports.description: The annual census of all city, district and regional councils and their non-market council-controlled organisations, and the Local Authority Financial Statistics (LAFS) compiled from it — the more comprehensive, less timely annual counterpart to QLAS. Stats NZ's own metadata states that LAFS is 'no longer published in the information release format used for 2009-13' and directs users to Infoshare instead, so the release exists as a data update rather than as a titled information release; kept as one node for that reason.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, released around May for the June year ending 11 months earlier. Distributed via Infoshare rather than as a titled information release since the 2009-13 series ended.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ publishes 'Local authority financial statistics' (formerly 'Local Authority Census') annually. No published forward release calendar entry was found for this specific release, but three consecutive years show a consistent pattern: released in mid-to-late May, covering the local government financial year ended the preceding 30 June (roughly an 11-month lag). Projected next release (Year ended June 2026 data) is therefore expected around May 2027; exact day not yet published.

reports.title: National accounts (income, saving, assets, and liabilities)
reports.description: Stats NZ's quarterly institutional-sector accounts, including the net operating surplus series that the Treasury uses to uplift company tax estimates in the Financial Statements of the Government. Named in FSGNZ 2025 by its exact release URL rather than by title — the most specific Treasury-to-Stats-NZ citation found this session.

release_schedule.note: Stats NZ states this experimental series has been 'published on a quarterly basis since the first release for the March 2021 quarter.' There is no published release calendar with exact future dates for this specific series, but recent editions show a consistent lag of roughly 13 weeks (92-93 days) after quarter-end (slightly longer, ~107 days, for the September 2025 quarter release). Next edition should cover the June 2026 quarter and is projected for around early October 2026, extrapolated from this pattern.

reports.title: Local authority annual reports
reports.description: The audited annual report every local authority must adopt under Local Government Act 2002 s.98, containing the information required by Part 3 of Schedule 10 (including, per clause 29, audited financial statements, and per clause 30A the district's rating-unit count and total capital and land values). Held as a class node — the exact counterpart of Australia's `au-la-annual-statements` — because Stats NZ, the LGFA and MBIE all name the class rather than any one council's report. `nz-wellington-annual-report` is this slice's specific exemplar.
reports.cadence_note: One per local authority per financial year, adopted within four months of 30 June (LGA 2002 s.98(3)).

release_schedule.rule: Annual report adopted within 4 months of the end of the financial year (Local Government Act 2002 s.98(3)); financial year ends 30 June.
release_schedule.note: This report's own url field pointed to DLM172329 (a section about combining consultations), not the deadline provision — corrected to DLM172354 (s.98) as part of this audit.

reports.title: Wellington City Council Annual Report (Te Pūrongo ā-Tau)
reports.description: This slice's exemplar council annual report, Volume 2 (Financial Statements) of the 2024/25 report. Chosen over Auckland and Christchurch on availability grounds: Auckland Council's site returns HTTP 406 and Christchurch's HTTP 403 to every non-browser client tried, while wellington.govt.nz serves the PDF to plain curl. Its Statement of Compliance and its Note 1 together close the New Zealand accounting-standard chain from the council's own side — see the `nz-pbe-ipsas-1` edge, and contrast Brisbane's refusal to name AASB 1049 in `au-government-finance.json`.

entries.covers: Annual Report 2025/26 (year ended 30 June 2026) statutory adoption deadline

release_schedule.rule: Under the Local Government Act 2002 (s98(3)), a local authority's annual report must be completed and adopted, by resolution, within 4 months after the end of the financial year to which it relates. Wellington City Council's financial year ends 30 June, so the Annual Report is due by 31 October each year.
release_schedule.note: The 2024/25 Annual Report (year ended 30 June 2025) was adopted by Council on 8 October 2025, within the statutory 4-month window. The next edition (2025/26, year ended 30 June 2026) is due to be completed and adopted by 31 October 2026 under the same statutory rule; the exact council meeting date is not yet published.

reports.title: Wellington City Council rating valuations and rates
reports.description: Wellington City Council's own published account of how its rates are struck on rating values — the New Zealand counterpart to `au-georges-river-rates`. States that values are determined by Quotable Value on a three-yearly cycle, that the process is governed by the Rating Valuations Act 1998 and audited by the Office of the Valuer-General, and that the council sends building-consent details to QV between revaluations. NOTE: the page writes 'Rating Valuation Act 1998', dropping the 's' from the Act's actual short title 'Rating Valuations Act 1998' — quoted verbatim in the edge basis rather than silently corrected.
reports.cadence_note: Rates are set annually; the underlying rating valuation behind them is revised three-yearly (latest effective 1 September 2024, next 2027).

entries.covers: Next triennial rating revaluation (effective date inferred from the 3-year cycle and prior 1 September 2024 effective date; exact 2027 date not yet published)

release_schedule.rule: Rating valuations are conducted every 3 years; the current valuation (effective 1 September 2024) 'will be the basis for rates calculations until the next valuation in 2027, regardless of any change in the market.'
release_schedule.note: Rates themselves are set annually (each 1 July, e.g. current valuations used for rates from 1 July 2025), but the underlying rating valuation that rates are calculated from is only revised triennially. Corpus's releases_per_year=1 with existing cadence_note reflects this annual rates-setting cadence built on the triennial valuation base.

reports.title: District valuation roll (general revaluation)
reports.publisher: New Zealand territorial authorities; certified by the Valuer-General
reports.description: The roll of every rating unit in a territorial authority's district, prepared and maintained under Rating Valuations Act 1998 s.7 and revalued in full at intervals of not more than three years under s.9. The rating equivalent of the Netherlands' WOZ beschikking and NSW's Valuer-General land values. Its statutory gate is unusually hard: s.11(2) forbids assessing any rate on the proposed values until the Valuer-General has certified approval of the general revaluation.
reports.cadence_note: Three-yearly per territorial authority (RVA 1998 s.9(1)), staggered across the 66 territorial authorities, so several fall due nationally each year.

entries.covers: Ruapehu District and Mackenzie District general revaluation implementation
Waitaki District, Waikato, Kapiti Coast, Marlborough District, Rangitikei District general revaluation implementation
Kaipara District, Invercargill, Stratford District general revaluation implementation
Masterton and Tauranga general revaluation implementation
Timaru and Westland District general revaluation implementation
Tasman District, South Wairarapa, Carterton, Clutha District general revaluation implementation

release_schedule.note: New Zealand's district valuation roll general revaluation is not a single national event: each territorial authority (TA) revalues on its own three-yearly cycle (Rating Valuations Act 1998 / LINZ guidance: 'valuations occur at least every three years'), certified by the Valuer-General. QV (Quotable Value), which conducts most councils' revaluations, publishes a rolling implementation calendar showing which TAs are due next. The image 'Revaluation_Calendar_2026_V1.jpg' fetched from the QV schedule page on 2026-08-11 lists the current tranche of upcoming TA implementation dates, September 2026 through April 2027, soonest first. Entries below group TAs by implementation month exactly as published; only some of the ~67 TAs are shown (those in the currently-published near-term tranche).

reports.title: Rating Valuations Act 1998
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand)
reports.description: The Act creating the Valuer-General (s.3), setting the Valuer-General's standard-setting, monitoring and certification functions (s.4), empowering the Rating Valuations Rules (s.5), requiring each territorial authority to keep a district valuation roll (s.7), requiring three-yearly general revaluation (s.9) and forbidding rates to be assessed on uncertified values (s.11(2)). Structural counterpart of New South Wales' `au-vola1916`, minted on the same convention that a periodically reprinted statute is a node when downstream documents cite it by name.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated statute, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule; version read this session is 'as at 23 December 2023'.

release_schedule.note: This corpus entry is the statute text itself (Rating Valuations Act 1998) on legislation.govt.nz. The consolidated 'as at' version is only reprinted when an amending Act or regulation takes effect — there is no periodic publication calendar or stated rule for revising/reprinting the Act's text. The current consolidated version is 'as at 23 December 2023' (last amendment date), and next reprint depends on whenever Parliament next amends it — unpredictable. Note: the Act's own Section 9 ('General revaluation of rolls at 3-yearly intervals') states that territorial authorities must generally revalue rating valuation rolls every 3 years, but that rule governs the underlying property-valuation rolls process (administered locally, staggered by council per QV's rolling revaluation calendar), not the timing of updates to this Act's text — so it isn't a valid stated-rule for this specific report/URL.

reports.title: Rating Valuations Rules 2008 (LINZS30300)
reports.publisher: Office of the Valuer-General, Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
reports.description: The Valuer-General's secondary legislation prescribing what the district valuation roll must contain, how sale details must be captured and coded, and the statistical rules a proposed revaluation must satisfy against market sales evidence (rule 5.5.1: coefficient of dispersion ≤ 12, median value price ratio 0.9–1.1, price related differential 0.98–1.03). Version date 1 October 2010; LINZ's own review page (fetched 2026-08) says replacement rules were expected to go to formal consultation in 2026, so this node's edition is likely to move.
reports.cadence_note: Amended rarely — Version 3.0 (2002), 3.1 (2003), 2008 issue, 31 March 2009 issue, 1 October 2010 issue. A review was under way as at July 2025.

release_schedule.note: LINZS30300 is secondary legislation (Rating Valuations Rules 2008) made under the Rating Valuations Act 1998, not a periodic statistical release. It was amended with a version dated 1 October 2010 (see https://www.linz.govt.nz/regulatory/30300). LINZ and the Valuer-General are currently conducting a phased review of the rules during 2025, intending to produce a draft for formal public consultation 'expected in 2026' (per https://www.linz.govt.nz/guidance/property-valuation/valuation-rules-guidelines-and-publications/rating-valuations-rules-review, last updated 2025-07-07). No specific consultation date, calendar, or fixed rule for future amendment cycles was found, so no computable 'next' date exists.

reports.title: XRB A1 Application of the Accounting Standards Framework
reports.description: The XRB standard that allocates every reporting entity to a tier and to a for-profit / public-benefit-entity track, and defines 'public sector PBE' by cross-reference to the Public Audit Act 2001. THE FINDING OF THIS SLICE LIVES HERE: XRB A1 never uses the words 'local authority' or 'Local Government Act' anywhere in its 43 pages (grep of the full extracted text, 0 hits) — like Australia's AASB 1049 and unlike the Netherlands' BBV or the UK's CIPFA Code, the standard does not name local government in its own scope.
reports.cadence_note: Issued 10 December 2015; compiled version read this session 'incorporates amendments to 31 March 2024'.

release_schedule.note: XRB A1 is an accounting standard, not a periodic statistical release. It is amended irregularly whenever the XRB conducts a targeted review or issues consequential amendments following changes to other standards (e.g. PBE IPSAS 50). Amendment history: issued Dec 2015; amended Oct 2017; May 2019; Feb 2020; Mar 2024 (PBE tier sizes); compiled to Feb 2025 (current version, effective for periods beginning on/after 1 Jan 2026); next compiled version through Jun 2026 effective 1 Jan 2027 (PBE IPSAS 50 consequential amendments). No fixed schedule or stated periodic-review rule with a computable next date was found.

reports.title: PBE IPSAS 1 Presentation of Financial Reports
reports.publisher: New Zealand Accounting Standards Board / External Reporting Board (XRB)
reports.description: The presentation standard for Tier 1 and Tier 2 public benefit entities, which is what New Zealand councils report under. Like XRB A1, it names no local authority: grep of its full 54 pages returns 0 hits for 'local authority', 'Local Government Act' and 'Public Audit Act'. The only local-government hook in its text is the word 'ratepayers' in the list of users of general purpose financial reports (para 3), which is not a scope binding. The binding is achieved instead by a statutory chain outside the standard — see the `nz-wellington-annual-report` edge.
reports.cadence_note: Issued September 2014; version read this session incorporates amendments to 31 January 2022 with further amendments effective 1 January 2026.

release_schedule.note: PBE IPSAS 1 is an accounting standard (not a periodic statistical report). XRB amends it irregularly via omnibus amendment packages as IPSASB updates the underlying international standard or NZ policy changes require it. Original issue November 2014; most recent substantive update is the October 2024 omnibus amendments (compiled to March 2025), effective for periods beginning 1 January 2026, with a prior amendment in May 2023 (audit fee disclosures). The XRB website states no fixed review cycle or forthcoming release date. The releases_per_year=0.2 figure on file (implying a ~5-year cadence) is not supported by any stated rule; amendment timing is genuinely irregular and driven by IPSASB/policy developments, not a fixed schedule.

reports.title: LGFA Annual Report
reports.publisher: New Zealand Local Government Funding Agency (LGFA)
reports.description: The annual report of the joint council-and-Crown-owned agency that raises debt on behalf of New Zealand councils — an institution with no direct Australian, Dutch or UK counterpart in this corpus. Names councils' own statutory planning documents as the material it monitors against its lending covenants. NEGATIVE FINDING recorded here: grep of the full 77-page 2025 report returns 0 hits for 'Statistics New Zealand', 'Stats NZ' and 'census' — LGFA's covenants are defined on accounting aggregates, not on any named statistical release.

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar or stated statutory deadline was found on LGFA's site. However, LGFA has released its 'Full Year Result and Annual Report' via NZX announcement in the last week of August each of the past three years (28 Aug 2023 for FY23, 29 Aug 2024 for FY24, and the FY25 report was 'authorized for issue' 28 Aug 2025), consistently ~8 weeks after its 30 June fiscal year end. The next (FY26) release is projected for late August 2026 based on this pattern; as of today (2026-08-11) it has not yet appeared.

reports.title: Funding Assistance Rates (FAR) Policy
reports.description: The policy that sets, once per three-year National Land Transport Programme, the share of each council's land transport programme the National Land Transport Fund co-invests. New Zealand's closest structural analog to the funding-formula technical annexes that anchored the Netherlands, UK, Ontario and Tasmania slices — and it is DELIBERATELY ISOLATED in this graph, because it names none of its four inputs to a titled source. See this slice's `_dropped` array for the verbatim negative. The isolation is the finding, on the convention `EU/G.47.md` established for `nordic-statistics-database` and `AU/G.1.md` reused for `au-brisbane-financial-statements`.
reports.cadence_note: Normal FARs are recalculated once per three-year NLTP cycle; the policy page itself is a living document (issued February 2021, last updated August 2023).

release_schedule.rule: FARs are reviewed every three years, before each NLTP.
release_schedule.note: NZTA states FARs are recalculated once per three-year NLTP cycle. The current NLTP (2024-27) runs 1 July 2024 - 30 June 2027; the next NLTP (2027-30) must be adopted by 31 August 2027 per NZTA's published NLTP timeline, so the corresponding FAR review/recalculation is expected before that date. No exact day is published for the FAR review itself.

reports.title: Accommodation Data Programme
reports.description: MBIE's monthly commercial-accommodation guest-night series, collected from accommodation providers and reported at territorial-authority level. Successor to the Stats NZ Accommodation Survey. Named by exact title in the Tourism Infrastructure Fund's assessment process as the source of the guest-night half of its eligibility ratio.

release_schedule.note: MBIE's Data Release Calendar (mbie.govt.nz/.../data-release-calendar, live-fetched, page 'last updated 03 July 2026') lists confirmed ADP release dates of 27 May 2026 (April 2026 data), 24 June 2026 (May 2026 data), and 29 July 2026 (June 2026 data) — all falling on the last Wednesday of the month, consistent with the programme's long-running (since 2020) monthly cadence of releasing roughly 4 weeks after month-end. Projected forward, the next release would be ~26 August 2026 (July 2026 data). Caveat: as of this check, the calendar page does NOT list any ADP entries for August through December 2026, even though it explicitly lists sibling monthly series (Tourism Volumes and Flows, Monthly Regional Tourism Estimates) through December 2026 — raising the possibility the programme's future beyond July 2026 is under review, paused, or simply not yet populated on the calendar. No explicit announcement of discontinuation, review, or schedule change was found via web search. Given 6+ years of unbroken monthly history and no confirming announcement of a change, this is reported as an observed-pattern (implied) rather than irregular, but the gap on the live calendar should be monitored.

reports.title: Tourism Electronic Card Transactions (TECTs)
reports.description: MBIE's monthly estimates of tourism spending derived from electronic card transaction data, published by territorial authority and region. Named by exact title and acronym in the Tourism Infrastructure Fund's assessment process as the source of the regional tourism-revenue eligibility test.

release_schedule.note: Tourism Electronic Card Transactions (TECTs) has been discontinued. It was an interim COVID-era measure (used roughly April 2020 to early 2023, with historical data available through 2024/2025) that has now been fully replaced by the resumed Monthly Regional Tourism Estimates (MRTEs) series. MBIE's own TEIC page states: 'The Monthly Regional Tourism Estimates (MRTEs) has resumed, and has replaced the Tourism Electronic Card Transactions (TECTs)' and 'No further updates or releases will be made moving forward.' MBIE's tourism-electronic-card-transactions reference page similarly says the series is 'Retained for reference only and not comparable with current tourism spending statistics.' There is therefore no future release to schedule for this report under its current name — ongoing monthly tourism spend statistics now continue under the MRTE report instead.

reports.title: Annual Report of the Controller and Auditor-General
reports.publisher: Controller and Auditor-General of New Zealand (Office of the Auditor-General / The Audit Office)
reports.description: The Auditor-General's statutory annual report to the House of Representatives, required by section 37 of the Public Audit Act 2001. Minted 2026-08-06 to close the branch's highest-value single gap: the corpus held no node for the New Zealand Auditor-General's own recurring output, which is what blocked the Tokelau half of the export-of-institution finding. The report is where the office states, in its own words and every year, the extent of its mandate, including the two jurisdictions outside New Zealand it serves.
reports.cadence_note: Annual and statutory. Public Audit Act 2001 s 37(1): "As soon as practicable after the end of each financial year, the Auditor-General must prepare and present an annual report to the House of Representatives in accordance with section 43 of the Public Finance Act 1989." s 37(2) requires it to include "an account of the implementation of the annual plan required under section 36" and "a list of entities audited by the Auditor-General under an arrangement in accordance with section 19". The 2024/25 edition is 108 pages.

entries.covers: 2022/23 Annual Report presented to House of Representatives

release_schedule.note: Public Audit Act 2001 s37(1) only requires the report 'as soon as practicable after the end of each financial year' (NZ financial year ends 30 June) — this rule has no fixed/computable date, so it cannot support a stated-rule entry. In practice, actual presentation/publication dates cluster in late September to mid-October each year: 2022/23 report presented to the House 26 Sep 2023; 2023/24 report signed 30 Sep 2024; 2024/25 report published 14 Oct 2025. The 2025/26 report (covering FY ending 30 June 2026) is projected for the same Sep-Oct 2026 window based on this pattern.

reports.title: Public Audit Act 2001
reports.publisher: Parliamentary Counsel Office (administered by the Office of the Auditor-General)
reports.description: The statute that constitutes the Auditor-General, defines 'public entity', and requires the annual plan (s 36) and the annual report (s 37). Minted 2026-08-06 because it was already load-bearing in this corpus without a node: XRB A1 defines 'public sector PBE' by cross-reference to it, Wellington City Council self-classifies under it, and the Tokelau audit mandate turns on it. Schedule 2, 'Specific public entities not falling within any class' (s 5(1)(d)), lists "Tokelau Administration" by name. A full-text search of the current consolidation returns one occurrence of 'Tokelau' and zero of 'Niue' — which is the sharpest single piece of evidence for the export-of-institution finding, because it shows New Zealand statute reaching into Tokelau and being silent on Niue, whose Constitution instead reaches out.

reports.title: Public Finance Act 1989

reports.description: The statute governing the use of Crown financial resources. Minted 2026-08-07 on Thomas's decision (planning/Decisions-2026-08-07.docx, option A: mint on arrival, and the minting session adds every edge it can verify with a direct quote in the same session, no cap, nothing minted on inference), closing a lead three prior sessions had deferred as 'probably the right next statute to mint' (NZ/G.4.md, following the Tokelau/Public Audit Act 2001 work). s 1A(1): "The purpose of this Act is to consolidate and amend the law governing the use of public financial resources." Requires the Treasury to prepare the annual consolidated Financial Statements of the Government (s 27) and the twice-yearly economic and fiscal updates (s 26O). Also supplies the other half of a bidirectional statutory cross-reference with the Public Audit Act 2001: s 2(1), "Office of Parliament means the Parliamentary Commissioner for the Environment (and that Commissioner's office), the Office of Ombudsmen, and the Auditor-General" -- naming the Auditor-General as one of only three Offices of Parliament this Act recognises -- and s 2(1) again, "Auditor-General has the meaning given to it by section 4 of the Public Audit Act 2001." Each Act defines a term the other Act's own scope provisions rely on.
